digest.component_or_area: plan review sizing and model escalation
propositions: When a context-limit error triggers escalation and the run's model is provider-qualified (e.g., bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0) but no class table is configured, the escalation loop returns a bare Anthropic model ID, bypassing the original provider qualifier.

The _rung_target function decides escalation targets by comparing provider-inferred forms derived only from the rung's class resolution, without considering the run's actual primary model, causing provider-qualified primaries to degrade to bare Anthropic family names.

A Bedrock-qualified primary escalating through the one-criterion retry receives a bare model ID (e.g., claude-opus-4-8), which composes into an invalid Bedrock model ID (bedrock:claude-opus-4-8) when cfg.model_provider is left untouched.

The fix threads the run's primary model into _rung_target and applies a provider-agreement rule: if inferred providers differ and the rung is not the primary's own rung, drop that rung rather than crossing providers.
When escalation stops due to dropped rungs, the existing too-big failure finding (_too_big) reports the outcome instead of silently jumping providers or crashing.

Escalation targets continue to come from the model-class vocabulary when a class table is configured, preserving the existing configured-Bedrock behavior and byte-for-byte back-compat for Anthropic and unqualified primaries.
